models.label: Parakeet CTC 110M (spotter)

models.note: The stream-N variants are the streaming export of the same checkpoint, one per published [left, chunk, right] attention context. The mask is baked into the encoder at conversion time, so each tier is a separate 591 MB bundle rather than a setting. N is the theoretical latency in milliseconds: chunk plus look-ahead.

The only row that produces no text at all: it says where speech starts and stops, and --segment vad cannot run until it is installed. No parameter count, because Silero publishes none for this export. The export stores some tensors at Float16 and some at Float32, hence mixed.
models.label: Silero VAD 256 ms (v6.2.1)

models.note: Hidden, not removed: an id typed in full still downloads and runs. FluidInference's int4 CoreML conversion is beaten by the GGUF build of the same weights on every axis measured, and is broken on M1-generation hardware. Against ggml.canary-1b-v2@q4_k_m over FLEURS (647 to 908 rows per language), WER int4 vs q4_k_m: de_de 6.96 vs 4.59, en_us 6.36 vs 5.04, es_419 6.03 vs 3.10, pl_pl 11.77 vs 7.19; RTFx 5.4-7.7 vs 49.3-63.1. Those are M5 figures. On M1 and M1 Pro the ANE compiler fails on part of the graph ('ANECCompile() FAILED' after 85 minutes, byte-identical on both chips) and leaves 149 MB of a 570 MB model on the Neural Engine: RTFx 3.7 and 3.4 GB of memory against the GGUF's 36.3 and 0.89 GB. FluidAudio labels the conversion beta. If a later conversion fixes this, unhide it - after re-measuring, on an M1 too.
